description: A primitive frontier cabin of split cypress logs, woven reed thatch, and bog moss chinking.
A small stone altar of stacked petrified wood blocks surrounding a polished agate anvil stone for flintknapping.
A semi-subterranean shelter with excavated floor, sandstone retaining walls, and juniper post roof.
A substantial dwelling of heavy petrified wood trunks with agate-inlaid doorways and translucent chalcedony windows.
A hillside semi-circular theater with tiered limestone seating and marble orchestra floor.
A multi-layered agricultural terrace with dry-stone retaining walls and gravel drainage layers.
An imposing mountain fortress with granite masonry towers, heavy ironwood gates, and multi-level saguaro colonnades.
A classic pioneer log cabin of hand-hewn chestnut timbers joined with dovetail corner notches.
A monumental stone stronghold with limestone curtain walls, iron-sheathed oak portcullises, and amber-inlaid throne room.
A grand chieftain's hall with heavy oak posts, thatched roof, iron hearth fixtures, and carved amber finials.
A folding bamboo screen. Divides space, lets light through.
A cypress timber outbuilding with bog-iron hinges and clay-moss lining for curing meats, paired with a kitchen garden.
An underwater passage lit by bioluminescent algae in the walls, with cave pearl markers. The Vorticist color in living form — blue-green against black basalt.
A heavy city defense wall of mudbrick core encased in kiln-baked bricks set in bitumen mortar.
A courtyard house of sun-dried mudbricks with bitumen waterproofing and reed-mat ceiling support.
A hanging chandelier of strung vertebrae and amber crystals, lit from within. O'Keeffe's skull against the sky, made into a light fixture.
A workbench with copper tools for cleaning bones — brushes, chisels, and wire. The meeting place between the bone and the keeper.
A carved limestone shelf for displaying cleaned bones. The first act of preservation — giving the bone its own space, its own light.
A narrow single-story home on elevated cypress stilts with mud-and-moss bousillage wall infill.
A fire pit carved into the cave floor with smoke channels cut upward through the stone. Amber crystals provide light, bone provides fuel.
A meeting hall carved from the rock, with gargoyle stone sentinels watching from the walls and glow moss lighting the chamber.
A sacred space carved deep into the rock, with gargoyle stone eyes watching, amber crystals casting warm light, and cave pearls adorning the altar.
A grand merchant courtyard residence with intricately carved sandstone jali screens and sandalwood doorways.
A simple carved niche in the rose sandstone cliff. The Subtractive Family's extrovert — the carving is visible, decorative, announced.
A sleeping hollow carved directly from the rock, lined with cave mushroom padding. The bed is the negative space — the building is what you removed.
Shelves carved into the cave wall, decorated with cave pearls. The Subtractive storage — the shelf is the absence of stone.
An entry chamber carved into limestone, lit by bioluminescent glow moss in wall niches. The first act of subtraction — removing stone to make a space.
A vaulted burial chamber with shadow moss insulation, bone displays, and gold-inlaid walls. The Klimt 'Death and Life' painting made into a room.
A burial niche built from ancient brick, lined with sound-absorbing shadow moss. The catacomb's first adequate resting place.
A magnificent multi-domed cathedral with imported limestone masonry and gold-gilded cupolas.
A fortified portal with heavy oak timber palisade, dry-stone limestone walls, and iron-strapped doors.
A traditional circular dwelling with oak timber frame, woven wattle, and steep thatched reed and heather roof.
A circular subterranean chamber with stone bench seating, central hearth, sipapu floor niche, and turquoise accents.
A tall stone cairn of petrified wood slabs topped with a luminous chalcedony crystal reflecting desert sunlight.
A covered public walkway with marble columns, limestone rear wall, and olive wood rafters with bronze trim.
A multi-story masonry structure inside a massive sandstone cliff alcove, with juniper beams and turquoise mosaics.
A traditional rectangular coastal dwelling of massive hand-split redwood planks on stone footings.
A workbench with iron clamps and a waxed surface. Where everything begins.
A spacious Creole residence with surrounding gallery porch, cypress siding, and hand-forged bog iron fasteners.
A domestic residence with sandstone foundation walls, papyrus thatch roof, and forged copper fittings.
A rugged terrace wall of interlocking granite stones without mortar, reinforced with ironwood posts.
An open-air solar chapel with sacred scarab altars inlaid with gold leaf and Libyan desert glass.
A walled courtyard of thorn vine and shadow wood, filled with nightshade and venom sac specimens. The Poison Garden's inner sanctum.
An altar that glows from within. The Fae Kingdom's sacred architecture.
The portal to the Fae Kingdom. Living wood, fae light, ancient bog oak, and tuned crystal. The gate between worlds.
A coastal lean-to of split redwood posts with heavy roof thatch woven from giant sword ferns.
A rugged wilderness homestead of notched lodgepole pine logs chinked with mud and geyser salt mortar.
A subterranean food storage bunker with fieldstone walls, chestnut framing, and oak plank trapdoor.
An elevated kiosk with carved sandstone pillars, stone cupola dome, copper spire, and indigo fresco accents.
Raised bed lined with willow and moss. Where things grow.
A guarded passage with gargoyle stone sentinels embedded in gold-veined brick walls. The eyes watch. The 64Hz Listener is present.
A gate of crystal and resonance that opens into the geode's heart. Requires materials from every level of the Inn.
A grand wilderness lodge with heavy timber joinery, geothermal salt-cured siding, and polished obsidian fireplaces.
A fortified entryway of kiln-baked bricks glazed with deep blue lapis lazuli pigments.
A monolithic four-sided sandstone obelisk on a limestone pedestal topped with gold-plated pyramidion.
A passage with gold veins running through dark brick, insulated with shadow moss. The Klimt golden phase as architecture — gold on dark, luminous against shadow.
A vaulted corridor with shadow wood beams, iron supports, ghost crystal glow, and moss-damped acoustics. The gothic architecture of the deep city.
An opulent two-story raised Creole mansion with colonnaded galleries, wrought iron balustrades, and honey-waxed finishes.
A monumental peripteral temple with marble Doric colonnades, bronze clamps, and copper roof tiles.
A grand multi-terraced funerary complex with limestone facings, carved sandstone colonnades, and gold sacred vessels.
A monumental multi-family longhouse of ancient old-growth redwood with elevated boardwalks and fog-moss insulated roofs.
A monumental multi-story Great House with core-and-veneer sandstone masonry, massive juniper vigas, and turquoise plazas.
An expansive mountain farmstead with chestnut log main house, oak timber barn, stone springhouse, and ginseng curing sheds.
A monumental multi-tiered stepped pyramid with mudbrick core, baked brick sheath, and lapis lazuli high temple.
A hexagonal living space carved around a basalt column cluster. The walls are the column faces. The chamber IS the geology.
A dedicated archery training field with carved yew bow racks, heather target butts, and oak pavilion.
A basic shelter of woven reed thatch supported by Andean alder framework.
A grand royal pavilion with cinnabar lacquered columns, copper dragon ornaments, silk canopy, and jade plaques.
A grand multi-tiered ceremonial platform with fine ashlar stone, gold leaf ornamentation, and imperial canopy.
A stone-and-thatch granary on elevated slopes with ventilated gables to preserve grain.
A bloomery furnace of limestone and clay to extract iron from bog ore, under a simple oak and thatched shelter.
An open-air shade structure with desert ironwood corner posts and flat thatched roof of saguaro cactus ribs.
A monumental rectangular hall with multiple trapezoidal doors, polished stone walls, and tall alder roof frame.
A monumental colonnaded sanctuary with massive sandstone columns shaped into papyrus-bud capitals.
A sealed timber log sauna with stone hearth furnace for generating intense steam.
A studio decorated with Klimt gold patterns — the alchemy of base material transformed into gold. The inventor's atelier at full power.
Bamboo cabinet with lacquered finish and copper hinges. Eastern elegance.
A single-room rectangular hall with central hearth, olive wood pillars, and limestone foundations.
A breathtaking ceremonial temple of fossilized tree trunks with fire agate floor mosaics and central chalcedony altar.
A domed ceremonial sauna of flexible lodgepole pine saplings banked with mineral-rich geyser salt.
A large dome-shaped timber-and-earth dwelling over four central posts, insulated with thick turf.
Fluted marble column with bronze cap and olive wood base. The classical touch.
A vaulted communal hall fashioned from bundled giant marsh reeds arched together and plastered with clay.
A towering octagonal Buddhist pagoda of fired bricks with bamboo scaffolding and gleaming copper spire finial.
A massive fortification wall of unworked limestone boulders bound with sandstone and bronze pins.
An ornate tomb facade carved into the cliff face, with copper and gold inlays. The Subtractive Family's public face — the extrovert who dresses for the audience.
A majestic northern-style Hindu temple with soaring curvilinear sandstone tower and copper kalasha spire.
Carved yew throne with runestone inlays and amber settings. The seat of a jarl.
A sturdy wall of oak planks sealed with resin. The basic building block.
A dome of star iron and cosmic crystal. Opens to reveal the full sky. The astronomer's crown.
A single skull against the window light, set on a gold-inlaid altar with fossil base and calcium crystal supports. O'Keeffe's vision made architecture.
A monumental multi-tiered wooden cathedral with massive corner pine staves, carved dragon heads, and amber-inlaid altar.
A wall constructed from bones and fossils set in limestone mortar, with calcium crystal inlays. The Sedlec Ossuary approach — death made architectural.
A prominent tribal lodge framed by heavy carved redwood heraldic posts depicting clan lineages.
A modest shelter with woven papyrus reed matting anchored to rough sandstone rubble.
A ceremonial wall panel of slab-cut petrified wood with geometric mosaic bands of polished agate and chalcedony.
Smooth pine flooring. Warm underfoot, fragrant.
A conical tripod framework of peeled lodgepole pine timbers, pegged with carved obsidian stakes.
A trellis of thorn vine and shadow wood that grows nightshade. Beautiful and deadly.
A raised planter for toxic plants, built from thorn vine with nightshade borders and venom sac fertilizer. The Gorey garden in miniature.
A personal crafting studio with shadow wood walls, undercity iron workbench, and ghost crystal accent lighting. The introvert's creative space.
A cozy elevated cottage on rot-resistant cypress piers with bousillage insulation and shaded gallery porch.
A conical purification lodge of thick fibrous fallen redwood bark slabs chinked with damp coastal fog moss.
Woven reed mat. The simplest comfort — a dry place to sit.
A shelter carved into rose sandstone with copper fixtures. The O'Keeffe maximalism — the form made ornate to honor the material.
A great round table of English oak. No head, no foot. Equality made solid.
An opulent palatial complex with domed chhatri pavilions, copper-sheathed spires, and sandalwood doors.
A storage chamber built from basalt columns, lined with salt crystal. The salt preserves anything stored within. The Vorticist functional aesthetic.
An above-ground masonry room of hand-shaped sandstone blocks spanned by heavy juniper ceiling beams.
A private retreat with bamboo framing, silk window scrims, lacquered desks, and carved jade inlay.
Strand of sea glass hung on copper wire. The tidal cave's decoration — the ocean's refuse made into art.
A traditional four-sided courtyard home with grey fired-brick walls, bamboo roof rafters, and red lacquer doors.
A sun-dried earth brick home on granite foundation, framed with ironwood lintels and saguaro rib ceiling joists.
Desert glass set in gold and silver framing within sandstone. Light made sacred.
Water-resistant cypress chest sealed with amber. Keeps the damp out.
A subterranean multi-story water reservoir with carved sandstone steps, teak bracing, and copper water-spouts.
A fortified canyon refuge against granite cliffs with ironwood palisade walls and saguaro-rib ceilings.
A traditional Southern Indian courtyard residence with teak joinery, sandalwood doors, and copper ridge caps.
An elevated terraced vault with bitumen lining and reed mats to retain soil high above ground.
A narrative wall — gold patterns shifting to show scenes from the archaeological record. The dead remembering what they were. The frieze you walk alongside.
The ultimate bone architecture — a cathedral where every surface is bone, every light is amber, every support is calcium crystal. The body's last structure made into the body's first monument.
A simple room behind the Inn. A fire, a chair, a cup, a book. Built from one of everything. The seed the Inn grew from.

The ultimate catacomb — gold-veined walls, gargoyle sentinels, bone displays, shadow moss silence, and ghost crystal memory. Death made beautiful. The earth holding you the way the tree holds the fire.
A greenhouse of shadow wood and thorn vine, housing the Poison Garden's rarest specimens, lit by ghost crystal. The Gorey masterpiece — the macabre made beautiful, the dangerous made deliberate.
The foundation of the Inn itself. Materials from every zone, every level, every biome. The building that builds all other buildings.

The ultimate creative space — gold-vaulted ceilings, iron workbenches, shadow wood walls, ghost crystal memory, moss silence, and geode crystal focus. The room the child eventually built. The room that was THEIRS.
The Subtractive Family's most adequate work — simpler than the Treasury, larger, higher in the mountains. The introvert's extrovert moment. The quiet building that is also the biggest.
The ultimate subtractive architecture — a cathedral carved entirely from living rock, every column a removed space, every arch a negative, the building IS the geology.
A forge powered by the tidal vortex's mechanical force. Basalt construction, salt crystal tempering, sea glass observation, copper workings. The Vorticist machine.
A monumental Hellenistic facade carved into rose sandstone, with copper detailing, gold urns, and desert glass skylights. The moment of revelation at the end of the Siq.
The ultimate angular cave architecture — a cathedral of hexagonal chambers, sea glass windows, bioluminescent walls, and a central vortex. BLAST and BLESS in stone.
An archway of living thorn vine with nightshade blooms. The Poison Garden's entrance — beautiful and dangerous, the Gorey aesthetic.
A shelter built from hexagonal basalt columns, insulated with tidal moss. Angular, functional, Vorticist. The cave's first adequate home.
Iron bracket holding a beeswax torch. Lights the dark corridors.
A cozy log cabin of horizontally stacked pine logs notched at corners, sealed with birch bark strips.
A bow-sided hall with heavy pine posts, wattle walls of birch, and insulated turf roof of moss and heather.
A heavily reinforced timber rampart secured with iron bolts and anchored on cleaved runestone blocks.
A sturdy shoreline timber shed with open gable ends for storing longships over winter.
A simple semi-subterranean shelter insulated with birch bark, heather thatch, and damp bog moss turf.
A stone-hearth forge under heavy timber frame, optimized for smelting bog ore into wrought iron.
A platform overlooking the central vortex, built from basalt with sea glass railings and salt crystal supports. The Vorticist viewing point.
A quiet chamber where bones slowly whiten in solution, lit by amber crystal. The last traces of organic color leaving, the structure becoming pure.
A sheltered river bridge with fired-brick piers and ornate bamboo roof pavilion sealed in lacquer.
A wooden church with stacked log walls, birch-shingle roofing, and an ornate helmet dome gilded with gold leaf.
A three-sided forest shelter of split chestnut logs and bark roof tiles with ginseng drying racks.
A communal multi-family longhouse with arched chestnut sapling frames, oak bark shingling, and central hearths.
A lamp post for the Undercity's narrow streets. Undercity iron frame, shadow wood base. The crafted light of the inventor's city.
An airy roadside tea house with split-bamboo screens, silk wall hangings, and lacquered serving counters.
